context: Recovering substitutions from occ-substitutions. Considering all possible GoI-execution sequences, we can derive unifiers thereby providing an analogue of Proposition 11. Namely we conjecture the following: ▶ Conjecture 36. Let σ, τ ∈ TΣ be terms, and suppose UGoI (σ, τ ). Let Γ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ denote a successful GoI-execution sequence for a pair of variable occurrences ⟨u[α], v[α]⟩, and let Γ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ M⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ be the overall occ-substitution generated along Γ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ , simply denoted by ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ MΓ in the sequel. Define the substitution ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ ( T ({M Γ (α) | ⟨u[α], v[α]⟩ ∈ R(σ)}) if α ∈ σ UGoI (α) = Γ⟨u[α],v[α]⟩ T ({M (α) | ⟨u[α], v[α]⟩ ∈ R(τ )}) if α ∈ τ , then UGoI (σ) = UGoI (τ ). Moreover, we further conjecture that, if throughout the GoI-execution sequences of Lemma 18 the most general occ-substitutions are always picked, then UGoI is the m.g.u. of σ and τ .
